```{r helper_functions, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}

# Show a GUI error message and stop the document immediately.
# Use this only for problems that should abort the current workflow.

show_error_and_stop <- function(message_text) {
  tcltk::tkmessageBox(
    title = "Input error",
    message = message_text,
    icon = "error",
    type = "ok"
  )

  stop(message_text, call. = FALSE)
}

# Normalize file/folder paths returned by tcltk.
# This removes braces and converts the selection to one clean character path.

normalize_tk_path <- function(path_choice) {
  if (length(path_choice) == 0 || all(is.na(path_choice))) {
    return("")
  }

  path_choice |>
    as.character() |>
    paste(collapse = " ") |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("^\\{|\\}$", "")
}

# Ask the user to choose exactly one folder. Stop immediately if no folder was selected.

choose_one_file <- function(caption) {
  chosen_path <- tcltk::tk_choose.files(
    caption = caption,
    multi = FALSE
  ) |>
    normalize_tk_path()

  if (identical(chosen_path, "")) {
    show_error_and_stop("No file was selected.")
  }

  chosen_path
}

choose_one_folder <- function(caption) {
  chosen_path <- tcltk::tk_choose.dir(
    caption = caption
  ) |>
    normalize_tk_path()

  if (identical(chosen_path, "")) {
    show_error_and_stop("No folder was selected.")
  }

  chosen_path
}

# Load an .rda / .RData file into a temporary environment and return the
# dataset object from it.
# This protects the global environment and makes sure only one dataset is used.

rda_to_object <- function(file_path) {
  temp_env <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())

  loaded_names <- load(file = file_path, envir = temp_env)

  if (length(loaded_names) == 1) {
    return(get(loaded_names[[1]], envir = temp_env))
  }

  data_frame_names <- loaded_names[
    loaded_names |>
      purrr::map_lgl(\(object_name) {
        get(object_name, envir = temp_env) |>
          inherits("data.frame")
      })
  ]

  if (length(data_frame_names) == 1) {
    return(get(data_frame_names[[1]], envir = temp_env))
  }

  show_error_and_stop(
    paste0(
      "The chosen RDA/RData file contains multiple objects. ",
      "Please make sure that it contains one dataset object only, ",
      "or convert it to a single-object RDS first."
    )
  )
}

# Save a converted or derived object as an .rds in the derived folder.
# This keeps a stable saved version of intermediate inputs for later reuse.

save_converted_rds <- function(data_object, source_path, derived_folder) {
  rds_path <- file.path(
    derived_folder,
    paste0(tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(source_path)), ".rds")
  )

  saveRDS(data_object, rds_path)

  rds_path
}

# Load an .rds / .rda / .RData file and return the dataset object.
# If an .rda / .RData file is used, also save an .rds copy in the derived folder.

load_r_object_file <- function(file_path, invalid_message, derived_folder = NULL) {
  file_ext <- file_path |>
    tools::file_ext() |>
    tolower()

  if (identical(file_ext, "rds")) {
    return(readRDS(file_path))
  }

  if (file_ext %in% c("rda", "rdata")) {
    loaded_object <- rda_to_object(file_path)

    if (!is.null(derived_folder)) {
      save_converted_rds(
        data_object = loaded_object,
        source_path = file_path,
        derived_folder = derived_folder
      )
    }

    return(loaded_object)
  }

  show_error_and_stop(invalid_message)
}

# Load a single CSV file and immediately save an .rds copy in the derived folder.
# This standardizes later processing around .rds objects.

load_csv_file <- function(file_path, derived_folder) {
  loaded_object <- readr::read_csv(
    file_path,
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

  save_converted_rds(
    data_object = loaded_object,
    source_path = file_path,
    derived_folder = derived_folder
  )

  loaded_object
}

# Load DCC from a folder of CSV files using the external dcc_csv_to_rds() helper.
# The function is expected to return either a data frame or a valid .rds path.

load_dcc_csv_folder <- function(folder_path, derived_folder) {
  if (!exists("dcc_csv_to_rds", mode = "function")) {
    show_error_and_stop(
      "The folder option was chosen, but dcc_csv_to_rds() is not available yet."
    )
  }

  dcc_result <- dcc_csv_to_rds(
  folder_path = folder_path,
  output_folder = derived_folder
  )

  if (is.character(dcc_result) && length(dcc_result) == 1 && file.exists(dcc_result)) {
    return(readRDS(dcc_result))
  }

  if (inherits(dcc_result, "data.frame")) {
    save_converted_rds(
      data_object = dcc_result,
      source_path = folder_path,
      derived_folder = derived_folder
    )

    return(dcc_result)
  }

  show_error_and_stop(
    "dcc_csv_to_rds() did not return a data frame or a valid RDS path."
  )
}

# Ask the user how a given input is stored.
# DCC supports folder-based CSV input, while the other sources use single files.

choose_storage_state <- function(input_name, is_dcc = FALSE) {
  choice_options <- if (is_dcc) {
    c(
      "Raw RDS / RDA / RData",
      "Already-cleaned RDS / RDA / RData",
      "Folder with raw CSV files",
      "Folder with already-cleaned CSV files"
    )
  } else {
    c(
      "Raw RDS / RDA / RData",
      "Already-cleaned RDS / RDA / RData",
      "Raw CSV file",
      "Already-cleaned CSV file"
    )
  }

  chosen_state <- tcltk::tk_select.list(
    choices = choice_options,
    multiple = FALSE,
    title = paste("Choose the", input_name, "input type")
  )

  if (identical(chosen_state, "")) {
    show_error_and_stop(
      paste0("Please choose how the ", input_name, " input is stored.")
    )
  }

  chosen_state
}

# Ask the user for the actual path that matches the chosen storage state.
# Folder-based inputs use folder selection; all others use file selection.

choose_input_path <- function(input_name, storage_state) {
  if (stringr::str_detect(storage_state, "^Folder")) {
    return(
      choose_one_folder(
        caption = paste("Choose the", input_name, "folder")
      )
    )
  }

  choose_one_file(
    caption = paste("Choose the", input_name, "file")
  )
}

# Load the selected input according to the storage state chosen by the user.
# This is the main entry point for reading a raw source file/folder into R.

load_input_data <- function(input_name, storage_state, input_path, derived_folder) {
  loaded_object <- switch(
    storage_state,
    "Raw RDS / RDA / RData" = load_r_object_file(
      file_path = input_path,
      invalid_message = "Please make sure that the chosen file is a RDS / RDA / RData file!",
      derived_folder = derived_folder
    ),
    "Already-cleaned RDS / RDA / RData" = load_r_object_file(
      file_path = input_path,
      invalid_message = "Please make sure that the chosen file is a RDS / RDA / RData file!",
      derived_folder = derived_folder
    ),
    "Raw CSV file" = load_csv_file(
      file_path = input_path,
      derived_folder = derived_folder
    ),
    "Already-cleaned CSV file" = load_csv_file(
      file_path = input_path,
      derived_folder = derived_folder
    ),
    "Folder with raw CSV files" = load_dcc_csv_folder(
      folder_path = input_path,
      derived_folder = derived_folder
    ),
    "Folder with already-cleaned CSV files" = load_dcc_csv_folder(
      folder_path = input_path,
      derived_folder = derived_folder
    ),
    show_error_and_stop(
      paste0("Unsupported storage state for ", input_name, ".")
    )
  )

  if (!inherits(loaded_object, "data.frame")) {
    show_error_and_stop(
      paste0("The ", input_name, " input must contain one data frame / tibble.")
    )
  }

  list(
    data_raw = loaded_object,
    already_cleaned = storage_state %in% c(
      "Already-cleaned RDS / RDA / RData",
      "Already-cleaned CSV file",
      "Folder with already-cleaned CSV files"
    )
  )
}

# Show a GUI warning message but do not stop the document.
# Use this for recoverable problems, such as rows removed during validation.

show_warning_message <- function(title_text, message_text) {
  tcltk::tkmessageBox(
    title = title_text,
    message = message_text,
    icon = "warning",
    type = "ok"
  )

  invisible(NULL)
}

# Log table for input-validation issues.
# Each row documents one removed problematic value or one input-level validation problem.

input_validation_log <- tibble::tibble(
  input_name = character(),
  row_id = integer(),
  column_name = character(),
  issue = character(),
  value_preview = character()
)

# Safely convert text to UTF-8.
# Values that cannot be converted can be replaced or flagged before further processing.

to_utf8_safe <- function(x, sub_value = "") {
  suppressWarnings(
    iconv(
      as.character(x),
      from = "",
      to = "UTF-8",
      sub = sub_value
    )
  )
}

# Validate a loaded input before any downstream processing.
# Logic:
# 1. detect text values that cannot be converted to UTF-8
# 2. remove the full rows that contain those values
# 3. log the removed rows in input_validation_log
# 4. save the cleaned validated input as an .rds
# 5. return a status object so invalid inputs can be skipped cleanly

validate_and_save_input_rds <- function(data_input, input_name, input_slug, derived_folder) {
  validation_result <- tryCatch(
    {
      if (!inherits(data_input, "data.frame")) {
        stop("The loaded object is not a data frame / tibble.", call. = FALSE)
      }

      data_with_row_id <- tibble::as_tibble(data_input) |>
        dplyr::mutate(.input_row_id = dplyr::row_number())

      text_columns <- names(data_with_row_id)[
        purrr::map_lgl(
          data_with_row_id,
          \(x) is.character(x) || is.factor(x)
        )
      ]

      invalid_cells <- dplyr::case_when(
        length(text_columns) == 0 ~ list(
          tibble::tibble(
            input_name = character(),
            row_id = integer(),
            column_name = character(),
            issue = character(),
            value_preview = character()
          )
        ),
        .default = list(
          data_with_row_id |>
            dplyr::select(.input_row_id, dplyr::all_of(text_columns)) |>
            dplyr::mutate(
              dplyr::across(
                dplyr::all_of(text_columns),
                as.character
              )
            ) |>
            tidyr::pivot_longer(
              cols = -.input_row_id,
              names_to = "column_name",
              values_to = "cell_value"
            ) |>
            dplyr::mutate(
              utf8_value = to_utf8_safe(cell_value, sub_value = NA_character_),
              invalid_text = !is.na(cell_value) & is.na(utf8_value)
            ) |>
            dplyr::filter(invalid_text) |>
            dplyr::transmute(
              input_name = input_name,
              row_id = .input_row_id,
              column_name = column_name,
              issue = "Value could not be converted to UTF-8. The full row was removed before further processing.",
              value_preview = dplyr::case_when(
                !is.na(cell_value) ~ "<invalid text>",
                .default = "<NA>"
              )
            )
        )
      ) |>
        purrr::pluck(1)

      rows_to_drop <- invalid_cells |>
        dplyr::distinct(row_id)

      data_validated <- data_with_row_id |>
        dplyr::mutate(
          dplyr::across(
            dplyr::all_of(text_columns),
            \(x) to_utf8_safe(x, sub_value = "")
          )
        ) |>
        dplyr::filter(!.input_row_id %in% rows_to_drop$row_id) |>
        dplyr::select(-.input_row_id)

      input_validation_log <<- dplyr::bind_rows(
        input_validation_log,
        invalid_cells
      )

      removed_n <- nrow(rows_to_drop)

      dplyr::case_when(
        removed_n > 0 ~ show_warning_message(
          title_text = paste(input_name, "cleaned"),
          message_text = paste(
            removed_n,
            "row(s) with text/encoding problems were removed from",
            input_name,
            "and logged in input_validation_log.csv."
          )
        ),
        .default = invisible(NULL)
      )

      if (nrow(data_validated) == 0) {
        show_warning_message(
          title_text = paste(input_name, "skipped"),
          message_text = paste(
            "After removing invalid rows, no usable rows remained in",
            input_name,
            ". This input will be skipped."
          )
        )

        return(
          list(
            valid = FALSE,
            data = NULL,
            rds_path = NA_character_
          )
        )
      }

      validated_rds_path <- file.path(
        derived_folder,
        paste0(input_slug, "_validated_input.rds")
      )

      saveRDS(data_validated, validated_rds_path)

      list(
        valid = TRUE,
        data = data_validated,
        rds_path = validated_rds_path
      )
    },
    error = \(e) {
      show_warning_message(
        title_text = paste(input_name, "skipped"),
        message_text = paste(
          "This input could not be validated and will be skipped.",
          conditionMessage(e)
        )
      )

      input_validation_log <<- dplyr::bind_rows(
        input_validation_log,
        tibble::tibble(
          input_name = input_name,
          row_id = NA_integer_,
          column_name = NA_character_,
          issue = conditionMessage(e),
          value_preview = NA_character_
        )
      )

      list(
        valid = FALSE,
        data = NULL,
        rds_path = NA_character_
      )
    }
  )

  validation_result
}

# Check that the user did not map the same raw column to multiple analysis roles.
# This prevents ambiguous renaming later in the workflow.

validate_column_map <- function(column_map, input_name) {
  if (length(unique(unname(column_map))) != length(column_map)) {
    show_error_and_stop(
      paste0(
        "Please choose different columns for the ",
        input_name,
        " mappings."
      )
    )
  }

  invisible(column_map)
}

# Ask the user which columns should be treated as:
# - original dataset identifier
# - cleaned dataset identifier (for already-clean inputs only)
# - article DOI, or "No article DOI column"
# This keeps the qmd flexible across differently structured source files.

choose_column_map <- function(data_input, input_name, already_cleaned = FALSE) {
  no_doi_choice <- "No article DOI column"

  input_window <- tktoplevel()
  tkwm.title(input_window, paste("Choose", input_name, "columns for the analysis"))

  intro_text <- paste(
    "Choose which columns should be used for the analysis.",
    "The full list of columns is available in the drop-down menus below.",
    "If the input does not contain an article DOI column, choose 'No article DOI column'.",
    sep = "\n"
  )

  tkgrid(
    ttklabel(
      input_window,
      text = intro_text,
      justify = "left",
      wraplength = 700
    ),
    columnspan = 2,
    padx = 10,
    pady = 10,
    sticky = "w"
  )

  input_choices <- names(data_input)
  doi_choices <- c(no_doi_choice, input_choices)

  dataset_var <- tclVar(input_choices[[1]])
  doi_var <- tclVar(no_doi_choice)

  tkgrid(
    ttklabel(input_window, text = "Column to use as original dataset identifier:"),
    ttkcombobox(input_window, textvariable = dataset_var, values = input_choices, state = "readonly", width = 30),
    padx = 10,
    pady = 4,
    sticky = "w"
  )

  if (already_cleaned) {
    dataset_clean_var <- tclVar(input_choices[[1]])

    tkgrid(
      ttklabel(input_window, text = "Column to use as cleaned dataset identifier:"),
      ttkcombobox(input_window, textvariable = dataset_clean_var, values = input_choices, state = "readonly", width = 30),
      padx = 10,
      pady = 4,
      sticky = "w"
    )
  }

  tkgrid(
    ttklabel(input_window, text = "Column to use as article DOI:"),
    ttkcombobox(input_window, textvariable = doi_var, values = doi_choices, state = "readonly", width = 30),
    padx = 10,
    pady = 4,
    sticky = "w"
  )

  input_done <- tclVar(0)

  tkgrid(
    ttkbutton(input_window, text = "OK", command = function() tclvalue(input_done) <- 1),
    padx = 10,
    pady = 10,
    sticky = "w"
  )

  tkwait.variable(input_done)

  doi_choice <- tclvalue(doi_var)

  column_map <- if (already_cleaned) {
    c(
      dataset = tclvalue(dataset_var),
      dataset_clean = tclvalue(dataset_clean_var),
      doi = dplyr::case_when(
        identical(doi_choice, no_doi_choice) ~ ".no_article_doi_column",
        .default = doi_choice
      )
    )
  } else {
    c(
      dataset = tclvalue(dataset_var),
      doi = dplyr::case_when(
        identical(doi_choice, no_doi_choice) ~ ".no_article_doi_column",
        .default = doi_choice
      )
    )
  }

  tkdestroy(input_window)

  validate_column_map(
    column_map = column_map,
    input_name = input_name
  )

  column_map
}

# ODDPub-specific filtering step.
# The user first defines which columns indicate "open dataset" status, and then
# selects which value-combinations should be kept in the ODDPub input.

filter_oddpub_open_datasets <- function(data_input) {
  default_filter_columns <- intersect(
    c("data_access", "own_or_reuse_data", "open_data_assessment"),
    names(data_input)
  )

  selected_filter_columns <- tcltk::tk_select.list(
    choices = names(data_input),
    preselect = default_filter_columns,
    multiple = TRUE,
    title = "Select the ODDPub columns that define whether a dataset is open"
  )

  if (length(selected_filter_columns) == 0) {
    show_error_and_stop(
      "Please select at least one column for the 'open dataset' filter."
    )
  }

  combination_table <- data_input |>
    dplyr::count(
      dplyr::across(all_of(selected_filter_columns)),
      name = ".n",
      sort = TRUE
    )

  combination_labels <- combination_table |>
    dplyr::select(all_of(selected_filter_columns)) |>
    purrr::pmap_chr(
      \(...) {
        row_values <- list(...)

        value_text <- row_values |>
          purrr::map_chr(\(value) {
            dplyr::coalesce(as.character(value), "<NA>")
          })

        selected_filter_columns |>
          purrr::map2_chr(
            value_text,
            \(column_name, value_name) {
              paste0(column_name, " = ", value_name)
            }
          ) |>
          paste(collapse = "; ")
      }
    )

  combination_table <- combination_table |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      .label = paste0("[n = ", .n, "] ", combination_labels)
    )

  selected_combination_labels <- tcltk::tk_select.list(
    choices = combination_table$.label,
    multiple = TRUE,
    title = "Select the value-combinations to keep in the ODDPub data"
  )

  if (length(selected_combination_labels) == 0) {
    show_error_and_stop(
      "Please select at least one value-combination to keep."
    )
  }

  selected_combinations <- combination_table |>
    dplyr::filter(.label %in% selected_combination_labels) |>
    dplyr::select(-.n, -.label)

  data_filtered <- data_input |>
    dplyr::semi_join(
      selected_combinations,
      by = selected_filter_columns
    )

  if (nrow(data_filtered) == 0) {
    tcltk::tkmessageBox(
      title = "No rows kept",
      message = "The selected combinations kept 0 rows in the ODDPub data.",
      icon = "warning",
      type = "ok"
    )
  }

  data_filtered
}

# ROAGG-specific filtering step.
# Logic:
# 1. if resourceType exists, keep only Dataset rows
# 2. if publicationYear exists, let the user choose which years to keep

filter_roagg_input <- function(data_input) {
  data_filtered <- data_input

  if ("resourceType" %in% names(data_filtered)) {
    data_filtered <- data_filtered |>
      dplyr::filter(
        stringr::str_to_lower(as.character(resourceType)) == "dataset"
      )

    if (nrow(data_filtered) == 0) {
      tcltk::tkmessageBox(
        title = "No rows kept",
        message = "Filtering ROAGG to resourceType = Dataset kept 0 rows.",
        icon = "warning",
        type = "ok"
      )
    }
  }

  if ("publicationYear" %in% names(data_filtered)) {
    publication_year_choices <- data_filtered |>
      dplyr::distinct(publicationYear) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        publicationYear_chr = as.character(publicationYear)
      ) |>
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(publicationYear_chr),
        publicationYear_chr != ""
      ) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        publicationYear_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(publicationYear_chr))
      ) |>
      dplyr::arrange(publicationYear_num, publicationYear_chr) |>
      dplyr::pull(publicationYear_chr)

    if (length(publication_year_choices) > 0) {
      selected_publication_years <- tcltk::tk_select.list(
        choices = publication_year_choices,
        preselect = publication_year_choices,
        multiple = TRUE,
        title = paste(
          "Select the ROAGG publicationYear values to keep",
          "(you can select one year, several years, or a range)",
          sep = "\n"
        )
      )

      if (length(selected_publication_years) == 0) {
        show_error_and_stop(
          "Please select at least one publicationYear value for the ROAGG input."
        )
      }

      data_filtered <- data_filtered |>
        dplyr::mutate(
          publicationYear_chr = as.character(publicationYear)
        ) |>
        dplyr::filter(
          publicationYear_chr %in% selected_publication_years
        ) |>
        dplyr::select(-publicationYear_chr)

      if (nrow(data_filtered) == 0) {
        tcltk::tkmessageBox(
          title = "No rows kept",
          message = "Filtering ROAGG by the selected publicationYear values kept 0 rows.",
          icon = "warning",
          type = "ok"
        )
      }
    }
  }

  data_filtered
}

# Prepare one input for matching.
# Logic:
# 1. rename the user-selected raw columns to the standard analysis names
# 2. create a missing DOI column when the user selected "No article DOI column"
# 3. run dataset_cleaner() only for raw inputs
# 4. keep already-cleaned inputs as-is
# 5. return both the renamed raw table and the cleaned table

prepare_input_data <- function(
  data_raw,
  column_map,
  already_cleaned,
  dataset_name,
  output_folder,
  is_dcc = FALSE
) {
  dir.create(output_folder, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  data_raw_for_rename <- if (".no_article_doi_column" %in% unname(column_map)) {
    data_raw |>
      dplyr::mutate(.no_article_doi_column = NA_character_)
  } else {
    data_raw
  }

  data_raw_renamed <- data_raw_for_rename |>
    dplyr::rename_with(
      ~ names(column_map),
      .cols = all_of(unname(column_map))
    )

  data_clean <- if (already_cleaned) {
    data_raw_renamed |>
      dplyr::relocate(dataset_clean, .after = dataset)
  } else {
    cleaner_input <- data_raw_renamed |>
      dplyr::select(dataset) |>
      dplyr::distinct()

    if (nrow(cleaner_input) == 0) {
      show_error_and_stop(
        paste0(
          "The input for ",
          dataset_name,
          " has 0 rows before dataset_cleaner() runs. ",
          "Check the previous filtering and the selected dataset column."
        )
      )
    }

    data_clean_col <- dataset_cleaner(
      input = cleaner_input,
      dataset_name = dataset_name,
      output_folder = output_folder
    )

    if (is.null(data_clean_col) || !inherits(data_clean_col, "data.frame")) {
      show_error_and_stop(
        paste0(
          "dataset_cleaner() returned NULL or a non-data-frame object for ",
          dataset_name,
          ". It must return a data frame with columns 'dataset' and 'dataset_clean'."
        )
      )
    }

    required_columns <- c("dataset", "dataset_clean")

    if (!all(required_columns %in% names(data_clean_col))) {
      show_error_and_stop(
        paste0(
          "dataset_cleaner() output for ",
          dataset_name,
          " must contain these columns: ",
          paste(required_columns, collapse = ", "),
          "."
        )
      )
    }

    data_raw_renamed |>
      dplyr::left_join(
        data_clean_col |>
          dplyr::select(dataset, dataset_clean),
        by = "dataset"
      ) |>
      dplyr::relocate(dataset_clean, .after = dataset)
  }

  if (!"dataset_clean" %in% names(data_clean)) {
    show_error_and_stop("The prepared input does not contain a dataset_clean column.")
  }

  if (is_dcc) {
    data_clean <- data_clean |>
      dplyr::filter(
        doi != dataset_clean,
        doi != dataset
      )
  }

  list(
    data_raw_renamed = data_raw_renamed,
    data_clean = data_clean
  )
}

```

```{r choose_paths_and_load_data, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}

# In this chunk we collect all user choices, validate all inputs, skip invalid ones, and create standardized source and DCC tables for later matching.

# Step 1: ask which source inputs should be matched against DCC.

selected_sources <- tcltk::tk_select.list(
  choices = c("ODDPub", "ROAGG", "DataStet"),
  multiple = TRUE,
  title = "Choose the sources to match with DCC"
)

if (length(selected_sources) == 0) {
  show_error_and_stop("Please choose at least one source to match with DCC.")
}

# Step 2: create a lookup from display names to compact internal source names.

source_slug_lookup <- c(
  ODDPub = "oddpub",
  ROAGG = "roagg",
  DataStet = "datastet"
)

# Step 3: ask where all derived outputs should be written.

output_folder <- choose_one_folder(
  caption = "Choose the output folder"
)

# Step 4: create the derived folder once so all saved intermediate files go to
# a consistent location.

derived_folder <- file.path(output_folder, "derived")
dir.create(derived_folder, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Step 5: loop over the selected sources.
# For each source:
# - ask how it is stored
# - load it
# - validate and save a validated .rds copy
# - apply source-specific filters
# - ask the user which columns to use
# - keep only the information needed for later preparation

source_inputs <- selected_sources |>
  purrr::set_names(source_slug_lookup[selected_sources]) |>
  purrr::imap(
    \(source_name, source_slug) {
      storage_state <- choose_storage_state(
        input_name = paste(source_name, "datasets list"),
        is_dcc = FALSE
      )

      input_path <- choose_input_path(
        input_name = paste(source_name, "datasets list"),
        storage_state = storage_state
      )

      loaded_input <- load_input_data(
        input_name = paste(source_name, "datasets list"),
        storage_state = storage_state,
        input_path = input_path,
        derived_folder = derived_folder
      )

      data_raw <- loaded_input$data_raw
      
      validated_input <- validate_and_save_input_rds(
        data_input = loaded_input$data_raw,
        input_name = source_name,
        input_slug = source_slug,
        derived_folder = derived_folder
      )
      
      if (!isTRUE(validated_input$valid)) {
        return(NULL)
      }
      
      loaded_input$data_raw <- validated_input$data
      data_raw <- validated_input$data

      if (identical(source_name, "ODDPub")) {
        data_raw <- filter_oddpub_open_datasets(data_raw)
      }
      
      if (identical(source_name, "ROAGG")) {
        data_raw <- filter_roagg_input(data_raw)
      }

      column_map <- choose_column_map(
        data_input = data_raw,
        input_name = source_name,
        already_cleaned = loaded_input$already_cleaned
      )

      list(
        source_name = source_name,
        source_slug = source_slug,
        storage_state = storage_state,
        input_path = input_path,
        already_cleaned = loaded_input$already_cleaned,
        column_map = column_map,
        data_raw = data_raw
      )
    }
  ) |> 
    purrr::compact()

# Step 6: choose and load DCC in the same way.
# DCC is validated first and only then mapped/prepared if it is usable.

dcc_storage_state <- choose_storage_state(
  input_name = "DCC",
  is_dcc = TRUE
)

dcc_input_path <- choose_input_path(
  input_name = "DCC",
  storage_state = dcc_storage_state
)

dcc_loaded_input <- load_input_data(
  input_name = "DCC",
  storage_state = dcc_storage_state,
  input_path = dcc_input_path,
  derived_folder = derived_folder
)

dcc_validated_input <- validate_and_save_input_rds(
  data_input = dcc_loaded_input$data_raw,
  input_name = "DCC",
  input_slug = "dcc",
  derived_folder = derived_folder
)

# Step 7: prepare all valid source inputs for matching.
# This happens only after all input files have already been loaded and checked.

source_inputs <- source_inputs |>
  purrr::imap(
    \(source_input, source_slug) {
      prepared_input <- prepare_input_data(
        data_raw = source_input$data_raw,
        column_map = source_input$column_map,
        already_cleaned = source_input$already_cleaned,
        dataset_name = paste0(source_slug, "_cleaning_steps"),
        output_folder = file.path(derived_folder, source_slug),
        is_dcc = FALSE
      )

      c(
        source_input,
        list(
          data_raw_renamed = prepared_input$data_raw_renamed,
          data_clean = prepared_input$data_clean
        )
      )
    }
  )

# Step 8: prepare DCC only if it passed validation.
# If DCC is invalid, create empty placeholder tables so the document can still finish.

if (!isTRUE(dcc_validated_input$valid)) {
  data_raw_dcc <- tibble::tibble()
  data_raw_dcc_renamed <- tibble::tibble()
  dcc_data_clean <- tibble::tibble(
    dataset = character(),
    dataset_clean = character(),
    doi = character()
  )
} else {
  dcc_loaded_input$data_raw <- dcc_validated_input$data

  dcc_column_map <- choose_column_map(
    data_input = dcc_loaded_input$data_raw,
    input_name = "DCC",
    already_cleaned = dcc_loaded_input$already_cleaned
  )

  data_raw_dcc <- dcc_loaded_input$data_raw

  dcc_prepared_input <- prepare_input_data(
    data_raw = dcc_loaded_input$data_raw,
    column_map = dcc_column_map,
    already_cleaned = dcc_loaded_input$already_cleaned,
    dataset_name = "dcc_cleaning_steps",
    output_folder = file.path(derived_folder, "dcc"),
    is_dcc = TRUE
  )

  data_raw_dcc_renamed <- dcc_prepared_input$data_raw_renamed
  dcc_data_clean <- dcc_prepared_input$data_clean
}

```

Successfully loaded the selected source dataset identifier lists and the DCC dataset identifier list.

```{r match_and_clean, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}

# In this chunk we match each prepared source input to DCC by dataset_clean, then create one combined table across all sources.

# Step 1: rename the key DCC columns so the matched tables are easier to read.

dcc_join_ready <- dcc_data_clean |>
  dplyr::rename(
    dataset_dcc = dataset,
    doi_dcc = doi
  )

# Step 2: match each source to DCC on dataset_clean.
# The result keeps:
# - the cleaned identifier used for matching
# - the original source identifier
# - the original DCC identifier
# - source and DCC DOI values
# - a source column showing where each match came from

source_matches <- source_inputs |>
  purrr::imap(
    \(source_input, source_slug) {
      joined <- source_input$data_clean |>
        dplyr::rename(
          dataset_source = dataset,
          doi_source = doi
        ) |>
        dplyr::mutate(source = source_input$source_name) |>
        dplyr::inner_join(
          dcc_join_ready,
          by = "dataset_clean",
          suffix = c("_source", "_dcc")
        ) |>
        dplyr::select(
          source,
          dataset_clean,
          dataset_source,
          dataset_dcc,
          doi_source,
          doi_dcc,
          dplyr::everything()
        )

      list(
        joined = joined,
        joined_dedup = joined |>
          dplyr::distinct()
      )
    }
  )

# Step 3: append all per-source matched tables into one combined table.

all_sources_dcc_joined <- source_matches |>
  purrr::map("joined") |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

# Step 4: also store a deduplicated version of the combined matched table.

all_sources_dcc_joined_dedup <- source_matches |>
  purrr::map("joined_dedup") |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

```

```{r save_objects, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}

# In this chunk we save all important intermediate and final objects so the full workflow can be inspected later without rerunning the qmd from scratch.

# Step 1: start with the DCC objects and the validation log.

objects_to_save <- list(
  data_raw_dcc = data_raw_dcc,
  data_raw_dcc_renamed = data_raw_dcc_renamed,
  dcc_data_clean = dcc_data_clean,
  input_validation_log = input_validation_log
)

# Step 2: add all prepared source objects dynamically.

source_inputs |>
  purrr::iwalk(
    \(source_input, source_slug) {
      objects_to_save[[paste0("data_raw_", source_slug)]] <<- source_input$data_raw
      objects_to_save[[paste0("data_raw_", source_slug, "_renamed")]] <<- source_input$data_raw_renamed
      objects_to_save[[paste0(source_slug, "_data_clean")]] <<- source_input$data_clean
    }
  )

# Step 3: add all per-source match objects dynamically.

source_matches |>
  purrr::iwalk(
    \(source_match, source_slug) {
      objects_to_save[[paste0(source_slug, "_dcc_joined")]] <<- source_match$joined
      objects_to_save[[paste0(source_slug, "_dcc_joined_dedup")]] <<- source_match$joined_dedup
    }
  )

# Step 4: add the combined match tables.

objects_to_save[["all_sources_dcc_joined"]] <- all_sources_dcc_joined
objects_to_save[["all_sources_dcc_joined_dedup"]] <- all_sources_dcc_joined_dedup

# Step 5: save every object as an .rds in the derived folder.

purrr::iwalk(
  objects_to_save,
  \(object, object_name) {
    saveRDS(
      object,
      file = file.path(derived_folder, paste0(object_name, ".rds"))
    )
  }
)

# Step 6: save the validation log as a .csv for easier manual review.

readr::write_csv(
  input_validation_log,
  file.path(derived_folder, "input_validation_log.csv")
)

```

```{r count, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}

# In this chunk we summarize how many articles and datasets were found in each source input and how many DCC articles, mentions, and datasets remain after preparation.

# Step 1: create source-level counts for each selected source input.

source_counts <- source_inputs |>
  purrr::map_dfr(
    \(source_input) {
      tibble::tibble(
        Metric = c(
          paste(source_input$source_name, "Articles"),
          paste(source_input$source_name, "Datasets")
        ),
        `Unique Count` = c(
          source_input$data_clean |>
            dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n_distinct(doi, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
            dplyr::pull(n),
          source_input$data_clean |>
            dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n_distinct(dataset_clean, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
            dplyr::pull(n)
        )
      )
    }
  )

# Step 2: create DCC-level counts.

dcc_counts <- tibble::tibble(
  Metric = c(
    "DCC Mentioning Articles",
    "DCC Mentions",
    "DCC Datasets"
  ),
  `Unique Count` = c(
    dcc_data_clean |>
      dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n_distinct(doi, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
      dplyr::pull(n),

    dcc_data_clean |>
      dplyr::distinct(doi, dataset_clean) |>
      dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n()) |>
      dplyr::pull(n),

    dcc_data_clean |>
      dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n_distinct(dataset_clean, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
      dplyr::pull(n)
  )
)

# Step 3: combine all summary rows into one table for presentation.

joined_counts <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  source_counts,
  dcc_counts
)

```
